Uriel's Chasm, at the time of this review, is listed as the worst game on Steam based on user reviews. "13% of the 1,092 user reviews for thsi game are positive," most of which are joke reviews about how this game is Uninstall Simulator 2014. For a game released three months ago, it's an incredible feat to already hit Absolute Rock Bottom.
This is why.
Uriel's Chasm is a multi-genre religious game. It starts off with an open space shooter, and then turns into a side-scrolling space shooter, and then there's a platformer aspect. The story involves heavy Christianity, where the main character is trying to ... actually, I'm not entirely sure what the character is trying to achieve. The game's mechanics are centered around collecting pages from the Bible, saving men from the crucifix, and destroying crosses that are shooting at you. Verses from the Bible are repeatedly displayed and voice-acted, but with no connection to each other.
The graphics are abysmal, not in a good way. I get that the game was going for an old-school style, but the quality is just horrible; it's like I was trying to upscale a 1990s platformer on my 1920x1080 resolution and they weren't meant to get along. At some points, the game kinda just looked disgusting, like someone threw up and published a picture of it on Steam. My best example of this is the greenish platforming screenshot on the game's store page. That's a pretty good example.
Gameplay is basic. There really isn't anything to say about it, because nothing incredibly stands out. It's nothing I haven't played before, it's nothing I haven't seen before.
The story and the voice acting are horrific. I never want to hear the voice actors in this game perform another video game like this in the future. The story doesn't make sense, and eventually resorts to just spewing Bible verses, none of which connect when they're given.
In summary, I don't want anyone to get this game. Please don't get this game. If you get it for free, start the game and leave it in the background for the trading cards. Don't spend money on it. Please.

The not-so-subtle meta commentary of the Beginner’s Guide goes from making you question what defines a game, to what defines art, to what defines the human condition, to what lies at the very essence of morality and interaction, all while staying true to the original premise for those wishing to interpret the meaning of the game literally. Its deceptively simple premise might seem linear at first– and many chose to interpret it this way– but as you delve deeper, you start to realize certain truths that have been rooted alongside the storyline. Without spoiling much, and for those who keep challenging me on this point, one has to look no further than Coda’s name to realize what Davey truly meant by making this game.
While I am of the cynical belief that people who over-analyze art do not understand the premise behind artistic expression, I am willing to accept the hypocrisy of the following statement: every single thought, meaning or realization you might come by while playing this game has been carefully set there. Any tangent your brain goes on has been designed by Davey explicitly to make you question your own beliefs. And as the creator of the most mind-bending game (The Stanley Parable) it is fitting that it is he who makes this title.
Through the Beginner’s Guide, Davey Pugh shows once again a level of creativity and intelligence that is so lacking in modern titles, and I would give this game an (8.5/10)

Red Orchestra 2: Heroes of Stalingrad is the follow-up to Tripwire's original hit multiplayer PC title, Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45, which has gone on to sell nearly half a million units since launch. This time, the game will feature a greatly expanded multi-player experience, with multiple new game modes, a complete first person cover system, destructible terrain, enhanced weapon mechanics and realistic WWII combat made truly accessible. In addition, the game will feature single-player and co-op game modes, allowing the player to play a full campaign from the Russian and, for the first time in a first person shooter, from the German point of view. Tripwire's renowned weapon handling improved even further, with new features and sounds. And tanks created with fully-operational 3D interiors, hugely enhancing the original game’s vehicle experience
Red Orchestra 2 is the best murder simulator I've ever played. It's not the best first-person shooter or multiplayer game, or even the best team-based multiplayer game. It's certainly not the best World War II game, and its singleplayer is the worst I've played in years. But in the killing, and in the being killed, Red Orchestra 2 is a terrifying and satisfying experience.
Let's talk about you for a minute. You're a soldier in either Hitler or Stalin's army, and you're♥♥♥♥♥♥scared. You've got your back against the wall in a room with one door, two windows and three walls, and you're peeking around a corner into the exposed core of a half-destroyed building. Every room could conceal an enemy soldier, and you've died a hundred times already, always from that one angle you didn't check.
Looking down through the rubble, you see an enemy soldier break from behind a wall. You aim and fire in a single motion. You've shot him and now he's dead. It's exactly like a million other games, but it feels nothing like any other game. It's the little things that make the difference, such as the sound of your own breathing when you lifted the rifle to your face, and the way it bobbed slightly in your hands. It's in the mark on your enemy's chest where the bullet hit, and the way his blood spritzed from his back, marking that bullet's exit. It's in the way he fell, forced by some terrible weight. Sometimes, but not this time, it would be the way he clutches his stomach, yelling in Russian, or the way he fires his machinegun madly during his last few seconds of life.
I highly recommend this game!

I adore survival games. I've played MANY of them in my time and there's not a single one I can say quite compares to zomboid. No matter how long I play this game, the constant updates and amazing gameplay keep me coming back. It has astounding replayability and so very many aspects that keep it entertaining on so many levels.
If you're looking for a tried and true survival game, look no further. Zomboid doesn't miss much when it comes to a true challenge and serious survival aspects. It takes things far beyond your standard "health and hunger" meter to much, much more, such as: thirst, mood (depression, boredom, panic, etc), rest, comfort, sickness, safety, strength and so much more that can come into play. Somehow, through it all, it manages to make none of these things an unbearable nuissance and rather an interesting element to overcome and make surviving in this zombie infested world all that more satisfying if you're able to last.
Sandbox mode offers you very many options that can make your game as easy or as impossible as you'd like it to be. It truly gives you the ability to maintain all aspects of the game you might be interested in tweeking, and where anything might possibly fall short there's usually a quick and easy mod you can use to get what you're looking for. However, as someone who has played as a *heavy* mod-loving gamer for many years now, Zomboid is one that I never really felt the need to mod, even after over 100 hours of gameplay. Though I will say what mods I've had a peek at on the PZ forums do look fantastic.
The world map is massive for a game like this. I didn't expect it to be so huge, but it really is. As it stands my only wish is that new towns get added soon. But one thing I love about the devs for this game is that they're *constantly* working on new features and expanding the game bit by bit. It doesn't seem as if they've slowed down, and reading the patch notes for this game is almost always exciting and chock full of tons and tons of new features, fixes and sneak peeks of what's to come. They're currently working on NPC's and vehicles and I know many can't wait to see that happen.
I could ramble for hours about all the great features of this game, but I highly recommend you, dear reader, to buy the game and find out for yourself if you're still interested or haven't already. There are many pleasant surprises and very few issues in this game that prevent it from being one of the most enjoyable survival experiences there are. Give it a go!

In a day and age where most games are pretty much the same thing over and over, it takes guts to do something different. Dejobaan didn't do something new here, but they did something completely unlike anything they have done in the past.
Combining bullet hell/curtain fire game play with FPS, Dejobaan have brought out the amazingly fun and utterly polished, Drunken Robot Pornography. There is no pornography in this game, however, there are robots, and one got drunk and started to terrorize everyone.
You are the owner of a bar that for some reason gives your robot bartender, Tim, sentience. Tim gets drunk and creates an army of Titans (Giant robots), which you have to destroy, eventually finding your way to Tim. You are joined by your flight suit named 'Suit', who you have hilarious conversations with, and you fight some robots.
The game is remarkably fun and very well done. It has some hilarious voice mail messages between missions for you to have a laugh at, and like with the other Dejobaan games, gets increasingly difficult as you play through.
Congratulations to Dejobaan Games (who have been bringing you quality video games for over 75 years) for creating one of the most fantastic games I have ever come across.

Reigns is really tricky in a wonderful way. It sets you squarely in a lineage of kings struggling to maintain order and balance in a kingdom with plenty of problems that are constantly shifting. There are four forces at play--the people, the military, the church, and the merchants--and they all must be carefully handled so as not to become too weak or strong for their (and your) own good.
The characters and interactions are fun, and brief but enjoyable moments of dungeon-delving and combat keep the experience from getting tedious. It's also surprisingly fun to intentionally start screwing up the kingdom to see just how your current king will be dethroned or dismembered.
If you liked Reigns, be sure to check out Sort the Court, a similar game that's completely free. Crusader Kings II will also be worth a look due to having a similar lineage system and lots of decisions and court-based intrigue, though it's a full-blown strategy game in its own right.

Meta as ♥♥♥♥, but tends to be illogical and too pretentious or trying to jam so much meaning and philosophical ideas in every chance it gets, and ends up being somewhat confusing and questionable game.
Minor Spoilers ahead:
The game itself is about finding out about a game developer's persona/life, into the actual narrator/game developer's problems coming out later on.
However, this is super anticlimatic at midpoint/ending and I found myself at first confused, but also at a distance/out of the game because the game itself is Meta, and the developer/creators/producers knew all about how the narrative will unfold. So, in applying Meta-logics and breaking 4th wall, they've essentially screwed themselves in terms of drawing the audience into the story and having them actually care about the people in the game. In terms of the story/narrative logic flaws, there are some things I can mention, but it's more or not up to the players' opinion.
The game itself does do a good job of being myseterious and entertaining at the start, but it quickly falls off as the narrative/game logic breaks, and being too pretentious and inflexible for interpretations. (Funnily enough, the developer wanted different interpretation and feedbacks, but all of it is already there, and all the hidden meanings are basically all told and shown) The game itself is trying to be too smart and thematic, but in doing that, the simplistic game mechanics also make it really easy for the player to just be told and see whatever is unfolding and what the meaning of it is.
It was a clever and intriguing idea, however the game turns into a big ball of diary and narcissism of unknown emotions and unclear motivations, that leaves the player confused or sympathetic, depending on who it is. The game itself is just unbalanced, and too narrow for one type of person, not covering even some portion of the others' spectrum.

You can walk away from those other games with a firm grasp on the progression of events or what exactly you've been looking at this whole time, which you absolutely can not say about The Beginner's Guide.
I look forward to seeing the 'walking simulator' genre mature, but this feels like a regression to rightfully maligned 'weird for the sake of weird' and 'lets play discordant music to make the player feel ill' games of the past like Dear Esther.
Maybe you might enjoy this game. Maybe you'll feel impressed with the 'twist' at the end which in retrospect is pretty uncreative. And maybe you won't start to feel exhausted by following micromanagment directions with no opportunity to explore and the game won't wear out its welcome.
Give it a shot. But not for $11.

Uriel's Chasm isn't a game so much as it is an experience. Unfortunately, if you're not of the age group to recognize that, or if you don't know this before you press "play," you'll give it five minutes, declare it the most horrible game ever made, and move on.
I'm going to flirt with madness here and tell you it's [expletive deleted]
. From the lack of a pause key or an options menu, to the midi-based music, to the absolutely brutal gameplay, to the lack of pyrotechnics, to the anticlimactic area "wins," to the interlaced, grainy FMV (that's "full motion video" for those of you who weren't around
its existence)...all I can say is just...wow. For those who didn't experience computer gaming back in the early 1990s (just as CD-ROM drives were hitting the market), Uriel's Chasm very accurately replicates the
experience of that era. Games were frequently nonsensical;  they often changed screens abruptly, they didn't hold your hand, they didn't provide tutorials, and they most
didn't have giant arrows or yellow question marks to point you in the right direction.
As an actual game, once you get into it, Uriel's Chasm is challenging, unsettling and even a bit disturbing. Part of the purpose of this game (other than to take you back in time in a very real way) is to discover each new section and how to play on your own, so I won't spoil those moments for you here. What I
say, is that it very accurately represents what were three out of the four main styles of gameplay back in those days (the fourth being faux-3D shooters such as Catacombs 3D, Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, et al), but skewed through Uriel's Chasm's own twisted lens.
Game play is brutal and unforgiving, but that's kind of the point. The controls are extremely responsive, if not initially intuitive. It runs smoothly even on my three year-old big box computer, and there is a solid logic or pattern to each area (even the seemingly unbeatable final level).
I came to Uriel's Chasm as an active Presbyterian Elder, curious about the Biblical aspects of the game, but that quickly became a non-event, as the experience took over. Nevertheless, there is some usage of Christian iconography that may be disturbing to some players (such as spinning crucifixes that fire bullets). Play time is pretty short but, as this is more about the experience than the actual game, that doesn't bother me. With all sincerity, and without any sarcasm, I tell you this : Uriel's Chasm is art. Most people won't agree with me. Most people won't get it. Most people won't like it.  I do. I do, and I absolutely recommend it to anyone who remembers what gaming was like back then and wants to relive the experience, those who are into hardcore gaming, or to those who are curious about it. All others should, as evidenced by the multitudes of negative reviews, pass it by.

Let's start off by saying this game is in no sense casual, it is for the hardcore zombie genre fans who want a challenge and who have been looking for a realistic zombie apocalypse simulator. I for one have been on the search for a zombie game that put all the elements of its predecessors into one perfect representation. From helpful but not over the top skills to the building that is not obnoxious but gives you versatility and creativity to create the zombie safe house or fort of your dreams.

This game also makes you control your charter completely from getting sick to going insane; you must not only build a base and survive by eating but taking care of your charter as if he were yourself. At first the game mechanics and controls may seem foreign but once you sit down and get to know them, they are very fluent. Talking more about the crafting system and various items in the game, there is not a single item in the game that does not have a use at this point, this brilliant plan of having every item in the game have its own specific role gives this game an immersion level like no other. Yes the graphics are not HD, but they execute the feeling and atmosphere of the game flawlessly, and could have been done no other way to give the game the feel that is has, on top of the amazing sound track that is simple and not too much.  The top down type gameplay with all the "weird" black space may seem odd and even annoying at first glance, but once you sink your teeth into this game and get familiar with the load out, it’s used and executed perfectly to again give an immersion level like no other.  I will say this, PZ is a game that is absolutely brutal and will kick you down and keep you there unless you play through it and get familiar with the game. Do not go into this game thinking you will live forever and never die.  One little scratch or run in with a zombie or two maybe even hordes of hundreds just because you shot your gun can be the end of you, after all the game tells you during the load screen that this  your experience  is a story of how you died.  On top of everything so far there is an amazing modding community that are coming out with mods and different maps to play if you eventually get tired of playing the two stock maps, the community as a whole is small but mighty with many active and helpful players.  I would have to say that this game is best played with a friend for an even more enjoyable experience. I could sit here and break down each aspect of the game and tell you all the amazing features this game has to offer, which by the way is still in early access for only $15 but no matter what I say you can never truly experience this masterpiece of a game until you sit down and write you own story.
If you would like to read up more on the mechanics and features of the game, feel free to visit the wiki here:
which explains all of the mechanics in great depth, there is also a sub reddit to get your questions answered.  Last but not least resort to this map of you ever end up lost in the world it is a lifesaver
This game is one of the most underrated games in steam and a once in a lifetime experience. The developers who put this together deserve a standing ovation and for you to buy this game, to help them further the games development process. I would have to rate this game a 10/10 for superb gameplay mechanics, and flawless execution of what surviving a zombie apocalypse would be like.

I picked Red Orchestra 2 up in the last great steam sale, and and my views of this game is incredibly positive. I'm not exactly the world biggest WW2 fan. But I have really found this game to be a pleasure to play. First thing, when you start it up. The main menu sound track is absolutely amazing. I'm been recently hooked on constantly listening to it for the last couple of days. And I am the kind of person who really in joys a good video game sound track. The game is very historically accurate, realistic, immersive. Which is all exactly what I like to have in an FSP. None of that casual gamers stuff like in Battlefield and so on. The game has a very large map variety and a lot of replay ability as well. And the game accurately depicts the brutality of war. And the more and more I play this game. The more I realise exactly why this game won the best game of 2011 award.   But I have to say one of the most funniest and rememberable parts of the game. Is when you jump onto the Rising Storm expansion and play as the Japanese. And when you do a BONSAI! charge, it is just so dam hilariously funny and entertaining. In fact in one round a was playing in Rising Storm. I did nothing else but BONSAI! Charges. No stopping and shooting or anything, just BONSAI! Charges. Even though that round I only got like only two kills. It was still an incredible amount of fun. But however in my opinion, Red Orchestra 2 does have its problems and issues.
First, the game doesn't fully explain all of it features and mechanics appropriately. Eg the ability to shoot enemies through certain wall and other objects. Or all of the expose week spots of Tanks for Anti-Tanks players. Second, moving around on the ground while prone, specially with an MG. feels kind of clanky. Third, you have to hold down T to see most of the on screen UI. Eg seeing how much ammo you have left. Or where your team is defend or attacking and so on. Which is really annoying considering I am used to playing the WWI FSP Verdun. Where in that game it's just a brief glance out to the bottom right or left corner to see your ammo and so on. And a few other small UI changes and things, that a won't further ramble on about. Also one final thing, on Rising Storm the ♥♥♥♥ing M2 Flamethrower is too ♥♥♥♥ing OP. I swear to ♥♥♥♥ing God, every single dam time. The Flamethrower really need to be nerved. But decides Red Orchestra 2 minor issues. It is an extremely good game, definitely a must buy. And I would happily recommend the game to other people. And very much looking forward to Rising Storm 2: Vietnam because of it. But if I was to give the game rating out of 10. Then I would reward it a 7/10. And yes i do acknowledge that the game graphics is getting really old. But I am the kind of person who literally doesn't care about graphics or anything. It's the gameplay which makes all of the difference.

Well I was skeptical about this game at first.  I generally check out the steam top games periodically to see if any highly rated games are worth my time.  This one was up there and after 5+ hours I can already see all of the reasons why.
This is survival done right.
I'm very happy that things don't wear out, which while I understand, it adds a ton of extra work that I personally don't enjoy.  I find it much better to upgrade your weapons and buildings to only be better than what they were.
The crafting system is simplified enough to where the basics are all covered in your manual. There is still some mystery in upgrading for finding new resouces that are generally easily obtainable.
Building is very straight forward and logically makes sense.
The AI is absolutely fantastic.  All games should take notes.  The AI does do some silly things like run into the fire (thank god for giving you somewhat of a chance for survival) so its not exactly perfect, but their actions and attitude are very unique, entertaining, and frightening at the same time, I love it.
Graphics are very good, love the godrays and day/night cycle.  While it doesnt reach the level of AAA titles its still very good while running well on most computers.
The story is intriguing and while isn't anything crazy, its much better than the Fallout 4's.
Multiplayer is so much fun if you have a friend to play with.
I still find that I enjoy solo just as well or at least close enough.  Your mileage may vary with that.
As far as cons/dislikes/or future wishes:
It would be great to add in digging of sorts and the ability to make tunnels and or trenches.
It seems as nights go on, plants and effigies seem to disappear.  I don't see anyone damage them, but the sticks for instance that the bodies are on vanish, and the body parts just stay in the air attached to nothing.
I figure its possible maybe they were destroyed by an enemy but, I didn't see it happen and since things just were randomly missing, it seemed more like a glitch.
It would also be nice to have some way to share a multiplayer save or have a dedicated server so you can return to your progress.  However, unlike ARK at least you have the saves on your machine so if someone comes and wipes out all your hard work, you can simply reload.
There is a ton of potential and I would only hope they don't over do it and also don't get greedy like pubg.  Once everything in the game works, I would however gladly play for a new scenario or map...once I finish the first one.
I would hope for more elaborate crafting however, that may need to vary on scenarios because it may not be practical with the current storyline.  I like the idea of Fallout 4's community and having NPC's join your cause.  I would hope to see that in such a game where they eat, gather...etc or the roles can be assigned.  That may be not needed at this time but, it would be cool.  Deeper crafting of course is always welcome, maybe not quite machine guns...I was absolute stoked! to see a catapault in the game! But primitive weapons even cannons or something like a musket would be nifty.  Older wood artillery would be cool as well.  As far as building goes, maybe something like windmills or things to create power generation may be neat, fire might be enough as well.  I would trust the developers to navigate that fine line better than I could suggest.
So the short story of it is, its a great game for a steal of $10 or $14.  I paid 14 and wouldn't ever look back.  You get a wealth of content and gameplay if you're a fan of the genre.  Multiplayer works and is super fun.  There are still some little annoyances but none to drive me to no longer play in the very short time I have so far.  I look forward to every day in the game and try to plan and make the most of it.  Its quite an accomplishment considering this isn't even the official build yet.
Keep up the good work Devs, glad to see you're active and appreciate your additions!

So Echo of Soul will be my first Review :)
Let's start it off with the basics:
Classes: There are 5 classes with 2 (3) different roles. There are tanks (Protector and Earthguard), DDs ( Rogue, Mage, Hunter, Berseker and Stormguard) and Supporter (Bard). Yes there is no healer, which gives you the control of your own healthbar.
Professions: Haven't looked in to it too much till now but there are primary (resource gathering, alchemy, juwelery) and secondary (soul something and cooking) professions)
Control: You use your mouse to target things and move your camera. Your keyboard is for interacting with npcs and using skills. So nothing out of the odinary.
Leveling: Leveling is quite easy. You can quick select quests with f, you have a build in questhelper and the first 20-30 Lvls are easily done. The longer you are in the game, the more you must be casious about your skills and need to find a good rotation to progress quickly.
Combat: It's a rotation and static based combat system. You cant move while attacking/casting. That being said, the Fights with bosses relies on heavy movement mechanics, which makes things really difficult sometimes. I like that system, it leaves it to you to optimize your dmg output.
PvP: 2 PVP maps, 5v5 Arena and Guildbattles at the start of a F2P game? Check! that's actually pretty big and well done.
Dungeons: You have lots of solo dungeons (every 10 lvls 1) which gives you the opportunity to equip yourself and have some fun thorugh the leveling process. There are group dungeons too, but mostly for lvl 60 chars.
Endgame: This Game has it all: good balanced pvp (no dimishing return right now, i hope they patch that in), lots of dungeon content, tiered equip, lots of dailys and professions to do. It won't get boring!
Difficulty: I would say you can compare it easily to Vanilla wow, which was for me the most challenging mmo experience I had so far. Most bosses punishing mistakes quite heavily and you won't get much help through guides because there aren't many out yet. You need to learn everything for yourself and that in an environment which is not forgiving to mistakes. For me it's pretty fun :)
New things? when you are ahead in lvl, you can warp yourself to a higher map without the need to walk.
Bad things? For not so talented MMO player its pretty hard, very difficult to equip yourself without help in the first tiers. You can be held in Stunlock in PVP forever. Your bags are to small. All the cool looking stuff cost (normal armor looks a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥)
Overall: I would recommend trying it out. When you get past the early 2-3 hours (pls don't hear on reviews from people with such short duration of play. They have no experience and just hate for no reason). It isn't for everyone, but it's F2P so trying it out would be the best choice for you.

This game isn't terrible but it could use a lot more work, like most Early Access games.  Good base plan: survive in open world where your only real goal is to escape.  I've always wanted to resident evil game like that, where you randomly find lickers and tyrants in the city and can run or fight.  Back to topic...  Good plan, lazy execution.
First, you can't go inside of buildings.  Just one question... Why?  In an area full of evil robots (or any enemies searching for you) crouching in the 2nd story window of a house and shooting down or throwing a bomb would feel great!  I understand this game is about being sneaky and hiding if you can, but that's even more reason to be able to go in building.  The general world doesn't have too great of hiding spots.  You need buildings to hide in and jump to and from just to get around anywhere that has more than one robot.
Second, any robot with a gun deals so much you are lucky to survive and patch yourself from the first shot.  Then, even if you do survive, you can't (to my knowledge) put bandages on your hotkey bar.  So, you can't instant patch yourself, meaning you have to pause and do it while they are still chasing you or else you will bleed out in about 10 seconds.  God forbid you get hit in a field or an area with nowhere great to hide, because you will get shot and killed while trying to bandage yourself.
Next, minor complaint: I do wish it was true open world.  I mean that the islands were all loaded with a render distance enabled.  Having to teleport from boat dock to boat dock is a little lame feeling.  I want the moment of running from robots, hopping on a boat and sailing out while ducking in to the boat and barely escaping in to the sea.  Then having the excitement of finding a new island and trying to find a safe place to dock.
I'm pretty good about going on for a really long time when reviewing games, so I'll cut it here, but I just have to say: Good start.  Great idea with the possible escape to try and give the open world genre some feeling of meaning, unlike games like minecraft which, while very fun with friends, can get dull fast when you realize all you are looking forward to is fighting a very laggy dragon that clips through blocks, to get an egg that does nothing.  But if this game wants to be remembered it needs to open it's doors (literally) and brouden it's scopes.  Also, not sure if this is a thing, but it would be cool if you could use hotair balloons you shoot down.  Patch them, etc.  Then be able to fly anywhere with them (again requiring a true open world).
Neat idea but plays like a mobile game and has way too much RNG to even remotely be considered a strategy or management game.

Let's start off by saying this game is in no sense casual, it is for the hardcore zombie genre fans who want a challenge and who have been looking for a realistic zombie apocalypse simulator. I for one have been on the search for a zombie game that put all the elements of its predecessors into one perfect representation. From helpful but not over the top skills to the building that is not obnoxious but gives you versatility and creativity to create the zombie safe house or fort of your dreams.

This game also makes you control your charter completely from getting sick to going insane; you must not only build a base and survive by eating but taking care of your charter as if he were yourself. At first the game mechanics and controls may seem foreign but once you sit down and get to know them, they are very fluent. Talking more about the crafting system and various items in the game, there is not a single item in the game that does not have a use at this point, this brilliant plan of having every item in the game have its own specific role gives this game an immersion level like no other. Yes the graphics are not HD, but they execute the feeling and atmosphere of the game flawlessly, and could have been done no other way to give the game the feel that is has, on top of the amazing sound track that is simple and not too much.  The top down type gameplay with all the "weird" black space may seem odd and even annoying at first glance, but once you sink your teeth into this game and get familiar with the load out, it’s used and executed perfectly to again give an immersion level like no other.  I will say this, PZ is a game that is absolutely brutal and will kick you down and keep you there unless you play through it and get familiar with the game. Do not go into this game thinking you will live forever and never die.  One little scratch or run in with a zombie or two maybe even hordes of hundreds just because you shot your gun can be the end of you, after all the game tells you during the load screen that this  your experience  is a story of how you died.  On top of everything so far there is an amazing modding community that are coming out with mods and different maps to play if you eventually get tired of playing the two stock maps, the community as a whole is small but mighty with many active and helpful players.  I would have to say that this game is best played with a friend for an even more enjoyable experience. I could sit here and break down each aspect of the game and tell you all the amazing features this game has to offer, which by the way is still in early access for only $15 but no matter what I say you can never truly experience this masterpiece of a game until you sit down and write you own story.
If you would like to read up more on the mechanics and features of the game, feel free to visit the wiki here:
which explains all of the mechanics in great depth, there is also a sub reddit to get your questions answered.  Last but not least resort to this map of you ever end up lost in the world it is a lifesaver
This game is one of the most underrated games in steam and a once in a lifetime experience. The developers who put this together deserve a standing ovation and for you to buy this game, to help them further the games development process. I would have to rate this game a 10/10 for superb gameplay mechanics, and flawless execution of what surviving a zombie apocalypse would be like.

Evolve is a game you'll either love or hate. Personally, I found it to be really enjoyable. It's a bit like a westernized Monster Hunter with guns. 4 hunters with different skills are pitted against a single player-controlled monster that will spend most of its time evading the hunters, and feeding, which allows it to Evolve into a bigger version of itself with stronger abilities. The Hunters goal is to try and find the Monster before it can reach Stage 3, which is its final and most powerful stage.
The Hunters have a range of abilities to find and fight the Monster, including a Mobile Arena that traps it within a confined space, forcing it to fight, and an alien dog that can sniff it out. The Hunters have different roles, the trapper, assault, support and medic. A bit like a Raid team in an MMO, each class needs to do it's job for the Monster to go down. A Hunter that strays too far from his group is an easy kill for the Monster, and even the wild life. The Hunters can bring down the Monster with effective team work.
The Monster is a single, extremely powerful boss monster that the Hunters must face, and each of the 3 Monsters also have a "role" of sorts, Goliath is the close-range berserker, Kraken is the long-range mage, and Wraith is the high DPS, low-health rogue. And while the Hunters have various ways to find the Monster, the Monster has various ways to Elude the Hunters, such as using its smell, and various traversal abilities such as massive jumps, flying, and warping across the map.
There are 5 game types, Hunt, Evacuation, Rescue, Nest and Defend. Though I'll just mention Hunt, the games main game type, which has the Hunters try and kill the Monster before it kills them, or reaches stage 3 and destroys the reactor.
There's also Evacuation, which is the "story mode" of sorts, it's a series of different game modes, and winning a round gives the winning team a bonus, if you win a match on the Weather Control Tower as the Monster, for example, more carnivorous plants will appear to eat unsuspecting Hunters.
There's also a single-player mode if you're into that, the bots are fairly competent too which is a big plus.
Overall I think it's a good game. There sadly seems to be some misinformation as well, however. To clear something up, the game is in no way Pay 2 Win, the only DLC as of now is cosmetic skins.

A great little indie survival sandbox. It's punishingly difficult, but it never feels unfair: every time you die, you know it happened because you got lazy, or overeager, or took too many risks.
This isn't a game about slaughtering zombies by the thousand. You'll definitely go toe-to-toe with the undead, but combat isn't the main focus—and half a dozen hungry zed are a real threat. It's more of an apocalypse simulator—in addition to fighting off the shuffling hordes, you'll be contending with sun exposure, psychological stress, spoiled food, and an overloaded backpack. You will die, and you will die often. But fortunately, as Dwarf Fortress taught us, losing is fun!
At the time of this review, it's in early access, so there are issues with game balance and incompletely implemented mechanics—but even in that state, it's well worth the asking price.

Here is my statements on the game as someone to whom bought it, not just played beta/alpha, I will list the pros and cons with my thoughts to help clear things up from people to whom are going to give you a review after playing just the beta.
So Evolve has had some poorly done PR, the DLC while cosmetic at the moment still rubs people the wrong way, which of course is completely understandable, but to the people saying why not just let you unlock it a lot of the major reviewers did not mention there is a master skin for weapons once you have done all the characters mastery to 3 stars.
Now this brings me to my first con of the game, Mastery System. Quite frankly its incredibly lame because it gives you a boost to that weapon/tool/monster ability its a flat out buff and forces you to do it, also you need to complete all the one star mastery's for each character to unlock the next, not hard just tedious as hell and it makes you play badly. For example I primarily play trapper, while my friends were on 3rd tier characters I was stuck on the first tier trapper because I did not need to follow the dog, it was just pointless so I started going into games and just following it without actually trying to play. I found a rather lame solution to this according to my friends by just going into a bot game to level up all the classes so I could play any character I wanted and not force the team to be at a disadvantage ( which isn't much because all the characters are good) but I still felt awkward.
2k and TR studios dropped the ball big time with a issue no one can talk about because it was not in the beta, Evacuation mode. With Evacuation mode you play a 5 day campaign cycling through different maps and game modes ( to which I will list) in order to save the colony and stop the monster, this is also a dynamic campaign so the next map changes based on who won or lost the last match. So for a Example I will list one
Weather Control (Map)
Hunter Victory Condition- The weather station comes online, clearing the sky's making the map brighter and forcing all hostile nocturnal wild life to not spawn for the next Map
Monster Win Victory Condition - With the weather station down a monsoon sweeps the area causing significant rain, making more carnivorous plants ( these plants will in-cap a hunter and force a team mate to shoot them out of it or they die) to spawn on the map, trust me there are a lot of those plants.
There are 12 maps right now, and not all of them are just dark jungle like what was showcased in beta, 12 maps with 2 different outcomes and 3 different game-modes that can be on them keeps the game fresh to me rather than just playing hunt all day like a lot of people have informed the masses after playing the beta, which again is 2k and TR fault for keeping Evacuation to Xbox exclusive in beta. Now moving onto game modes we have 4 different games modes one having its own map set Ill list them below
Hunt- Standard mode that was showcased in beta, can be fun and exhilarating, or can be a wild goose chase (looking at your wraith)
Nest there are 6 monster eggs on the map, the hunters must kill all the eggs and the monster must defend them, he may also hatch an egg to make a baby Goliath to help defend, but if the Goliath is killed it will count as a kill for the hunter, this is by far my favorite game mode, it makes it to where its a race to kill as many eggs and has a lot of tactics behind it i.e splitting up to go faster so he doesn't get stage 3 strategic picks on hunter ( one of the hunters has mines, another has turrets etc.)
Rescue- by far my least favorite because of how its spaced out, the hunters need to rescue 5 civilians to whom are down on the ground and protect them until a drop-ship arrives, the monster must kill 5. I feel as though this mode was made a little poorly, since the survivors spawn 2,2,5 so the monster doesn't really have to bother with the first 2 sets and can instead just rush to level 3 to wipe out the poor colonists because there skin is made of paper and their bones balsa wood.
Defend- Last game-mode of every evacuation campaign Monster starts at level 3 and must destroy 3 power relays, the hunters must defend the relays for 6 minutes using the given destructible turrets, or kill the alpha monster (player controlled one) every 45 seconds a wave of 2 AI controlled monster minions spawn and go straight for the relay and will only stop attacking it when they are at 25% health or below,the monster can play this out like a MOBA i.e go for the turrets with ranged attacks or melee them while the hunters are distracted with the minions, each relay the monster kills till his final one adds 5 minutes to the clock. Monster perk for winning the 4th map, his minions have armor which make them even harder to kill since the turrets suck without the buff. Hunter perk- Turrets get the mentioned buff making them chew through monsters and minions, so both perks are pretty good, I rate the monsters better though
Last point of evacuation mode to which I am torn on is, each time one side wins, they get the map buff while the losing side gets 10% damage, which is that losing side wins it takes down one bar of the buff of 5 so for example winning the first map as the hunters you get the weather buff, but the monster gets 10% damage, he uses this damage to win the next map then goes back down to 0% buff, so its a bit of a tug of war with winning and losing to ensure fair play, so why am I torn? It creates a lot of cheese Strats, because using the damage boost you can just effectively kill the hunters level one with one of the monsters then go on the win the last mission using the 30% damage boost and super minions.
Now we get to the question, is the game worth 60$ dollars? Well if you have been reading my overview with how much I've shown you, I'm going to say to the standard person, No. To some people money is tight and things like this cannot fly for them, its understandable to for some people it is just way to much, I agree that it should of been 30 or 40$! For my personally I feel as though I've gotten my moneys worth though, I enjoy playing the game, love the character design and banter, and have over all loved playing the game with friends and pubs alike. What it comes down to is, its a fun fleshed out game that's getting a lot of PR problems ,circle-jerking from people whom have not played it or played the betas one game mode, Which I understand people want it to fail, but there are people who enjoy it please be mindful of that.

How do I explain this one? Well, first off, there's alcohol and robots, but no porn to speak of. The game starts off fairly easy, but it quickly gets harder and harder, becoming as challenging as you'd expect a first-person bullet hell game to be. The visuals and soundtrack are excellent, the controls are solid, and the battles are simple but very adrenalin-pumping.
Long story short, you're an unlucky bar owner who happened to end up giving his robot bartender sentience, causing him to go on a rampage, burn down your bar, and destroy the city. Oh, and he ganked your other robots. So now you're travelling the city with the help of Suit, an uplifted starfish connected to...well, your suit (as all robotics have gone rogue), and you're going around destroying drones, blasting apart huge Titans piece by piece, and collecting martinis and cocktail mixers along the way. There doesn't seem to be much in the way of serious plot, just quirky details and comical moments all 'round.
As far as what you have, all you get is your jetpack and your gun. You can pick up things to power those things up, though you can also get things like the Smart Bomb, invulnerability, or even a rainbow-hued death ray from the sky.
Finally, the game has two deep and open-ended editors, one for building your own giant robots and one for building maps to put those awesome monstrosities in (or not). There's enough creativity in the Workshop to make looking around worth the trouble.
Potential turn-offs for some people include the crazy difficulty (which can be mitigated somewhat by the game's own Easy difficulty), the style of humor used, the fact that gameplay tends to stick to a certain formula, and the lack of actual porn. None of those bother me, though.
Overall, if you enjoy bullet hell, first-person shooters, and/or giant robots, you should look into this game.

Unlocking the frame rate:
Locate the ROEngine.ini inside: "C:\Users\User\Documents\My Games\RedOrchestra2\ROGame\Config" open ROEngine with Notepad.
Locate a parameter that looks like this:
bSmoothFrameRate=TRUE
MinSmoothedFrameRate=22
MaxSmoothedFrameRate=62
Set "MaxSmoothedFrameRate=62" to "MaxSmoothedFrameRate=144" - I've used 144 as an example.
Note: Setting "bSmoothFrameRate=FALSE" will uncap the limit but you will only be able to get 90 frames.
Find the remaining MaxSmoothedFrameRate lines (use Ctrl + f) and set their values to the desired amount (there are 2 MaxSmoothedFrameRate and 2 bSmoothFrameRate to edit).
Now test using either the steam FPS overlay or alternatively open the console ingame with "~" and type in "Stat FPS".

Forward to the Sky is a very anime-styled 3D platformer with a cute story marred by somewhat awful voice acting and equally bad combat mechanics.
As far as the actual platforming goes, it's not terrible, though it's got a good few tricky puzzles if you want to break all three statues on each level in order to see the entire story, which I'd recommend since it's pretty adorable. The remainder of the crystals on each level are gotten by fighting crystal skeletons, and the mechanics for that are honestly pretty terrible. Thankfully, the game never requires you to get all that good at it, because there's a limited and rather low amount of enemies on each level.
Ultimately, it's also rather short - six levels, each of which can be completed rather quickly if you're just trying to finish them, and it only took me two hours to find all of the statues hidden in the first five. As such, the price (currently $8) feels a little high, and it ends up not really having much of a "draw" since there are plenty of other 3D platformers and cute anime-styled games out there, with this one not really boasting any unique features.

Not overly impressed after enjoying it's predecessor SH3 for so long. Funny way to start recommending  a product but I am still in the hospital drying my wet clothes ............
because;
I just traversed the width of the pacific from the south china seas with 70,000 tons to my credit on first patrol, set course back to Pearl saved, used time compression and destroyed the boat running into Hawaii. (last saved in the South China seas) Is there no return to base option? If so I cannot see one! When I approached Surabaya in the same fashion it asked me if I wanted to refit there! (maybe I was speeding this time:D)
Overall I enjoyed the patrol itself (to be fair), however the Porpoise class sub seems to run high in the water and takes too long to crash dive on alarm as the approaching nme aircraft seem to be escaping the eyes of the 'ever alert' watch on deck and drop countless bombs immediately and accurately. This sub has a deck gun at the rear of the conning tower which I will never understand in it's design and nor would a hundred other Admirals, you have to juxta position your boat for a surface gunnery attack which can be extremely dangerous in many ways!
There is a submerged safety factor from depth charging although unfortunately, repetitive at 50+ metres depth ('passing thermal layer') which is a little unrealistic as it seems to occur repeatedly. Also as I said the aircraft seem to carry an enormous amount of ordnance to drop on you instead of the usual two or so that a f/bomber would carry. It could be the amount of realism set in options perhaps but puts it in the 'arcade' genre when this part of the action happens if not.
The crew SHOUT or YELL orders emotionally (similar to SH3) which no skipper I am sure would tolerate especially during the critical phases of battle. (turn down the voices  seems to help as you work out your moves).

Three torpedoes successfully into a small old freighter, a quick surface and use ten rounds of HE and AP onto her and still she is not sinking and has headway at a 5O degree list and on fire ...yeah right! Oh hang on she just called up the Imperial Japanese airforce with their ten bombs each and they have immediately arrived!
The message clipboard is tedious even after you send your status reports and old news just sits there unfiltered. SH3 BDU naval message was more exact and relevant for the skipper's info and tactics etc.
You can add your 78's to the gramophone again which is excellent! (What's a '78' ?....look it up)!
It's open world of course, a vast canvas with random friendlies and nme battle groups etc, don't try land like I did, you don't have wheels!
Excellent UI easy to understand and use even on your first mission, all of the controls are important to attack and survival, logical, weather and seascape is excellent as are the models of ships. There is a lot of plankton. The Pacific Ocean is very big!
All in all for me it's 7.5/10 because it has an editor attached which has to keep the interest; it's good fun and perhaps if you are a true purist of the subsim sort then the higher realism options may increase your enjoyment. $20 sounds fair for the scope of the product, it's replay ability and graphic qualities. It has depth (haha) and worthwhile to spend time on despite it's shortcomings and with mods of course it's expansive.

When you play a text-based game & after awhile find yourself reluctant to read the incoming 2-liners, then you might suspect something is wrong with the affair. This game is crap, it is not done to the point where it would have become truly a game. It's just a mobile gimmick to spend 20 minutes in transport, nothing more.
I'm a fan of text-based gameplay, games like "King of Dragon Pass" & "NEOScavenger" (where explicit tactical process is texted to you) truly amase me, so I probably hoped for a little too much in case of this micro-strategy. "Reigns" borrows inspiration from "Hot or Not" kind of web services - a random card of a court person or an ambassador appears before you & tells something more or less relevant, you then sway your mouse to the sides & see the 2 reaction options (negative & positive generally) & roughly the possible effects they would have on the 4 main parameters which you try balancing all the time - the relative weights of 4 social castes in the society: Clergy, People, Military, Finance. If any of the 4 parameters gets to the maximum or the minimum another poor monarch will pass. Simply cool, right? Wrong.
It's not fun. Balance or not, the kings go really soon (of old age for example). You are not a king, you play as some kind of a guardian angel of the monarchy - kings will die, die & die, John XVIII will succeed to the crown of Nebuchadnezzar XXXIV while you insensibly quit paying attention to their individual fates, for you have seen everything that might happen to them 200 times already during this very gameplay session, even the picturesque deaths repeat, humour vanishes. Critical situations like wars & epidemics will come & go taking the balance & your avatars with them, while you'll still be trying to accomplish some unknown conditions to get a 2 thousand years old quests done. That's the true point of the game - to get a series of story quests (you can't care less about) done through guessing right answers at some tricky situations. Then you might even get a new pack of cards, which will repeat themselves for another 2k yrs of this. A decision is made every year, kings get old quick, the gameplay even quicker so.
Ask yourself for how many times are you willing to read the same paragraph of the most interesting book just to push through? And don't expect much here!

I really wish steam had a neutral rating.  This isn't a bad game, but at just 2 hours it is incredibly small for the price.  It has one concept (time only moves when you move, which isn't actually true; enemies and bullets still move even when standing still, just very slowly), but it doesn't do much with it.  The campaign levels are short, and the challenge levels all happen in the same arena.  The tiny story tries to be artsy and profound but comes across as just vague nonsense.  I have a feeling it was made for the VR platform and a lot is lost when playing on PC.
The game is also headache-inducing because the environment is predominately white, and there is very little to break that up.  Movement is slow and herky-jerky, which makes manuvering painfully frustrating, but it's required because levels are designed so you can't take two steps without being in someone's line of fire, and the game requires precision movement to dodge enemies and bullets.  The levels are disconnected and have nothing to do with one another, which doesn't help the story at all because it doesn't feel like a coherent whole.
The developers had a decent idea, and I think it could have been better if the story mode had been better.  Without that, everything is kinda pointless.  It's not bad as a proof-of-concept, as the gameplay is challenging, satisfying, and stands on its own, but a single gimmick can only take a game so far.

Here sits another game where I'm mostly on the fence about recommending it.  Ultimately though, I'd have to say it's a soft pass as the gameplay itself is rather "blah"
In essence, you rule a kingdom in some weird Tinder-style manner of swiping "cards" left or right.  It's kind of a stat management game? Yes, that's an intentional question mark.  You do have 4 icons across the top of the cards that represent the different factions that you must keep happy in order to be not dead. Your actions (left/right swipes) have positive or negative effects on one or multiple groups.  That's basically it. Oh, and when you do die (it happens a lot), you take over as your heir.  Not sure why you always HAVE an heir, as there were times I messed up and died within 3 years or so. But whatevs. Either way, you plod along.
At first, it was fairly entertaining and when random events would pop up, I would gain a new "card set" that adds more events and triggers.  But after awhile (and many, many ruler's deaths) I felt as though I was recycling the exact same cards in the exact same situations and quickly grew bored.
On the positive side, the minimalistic art style is nice.  And the price is about right.  But if you subscribe to the thought that each dollar = an hour of play, then I ran out at about $1.50.
If nothing else, it's a good start. But I'd say pass unless you gain this in a bundle or a deep discount (as it's already inexpensive).

All my friends, my family, my colleagues turned into these terrible, mindless creatures that run after me and just have one thing in their minds: to disembowel me. Why am I still alive at all? It just doesn't make any sense to me.
I need to leave our...I mean my house, all windows are broken and these monsters are just awaiting the moment I fall asleep to get me.
I just found out that my neighbors fled to the north as I'm reading their note directed to their daughter who was expected to come home from college. I found her, in pieces on the floor and wallpaper. What a tragedy, she was so beautiful and smart.
I knew her dad likes to drink so I took his whiskey and a few blankets. Maybe they get handy one day.
I found a house to live in; but I don't feel safe- I need more blankets to disguise the windows. Luckily, the former owner had a good storage of food.
Ok, I will f***ing leave... just needed to kill five zombies- this area is polluted with these rats an I was wounded on my right hand.
Used the whisky to disinfect and blankets to bandage. Hopefully, it will help.... hopefully? Or isn't it better to die? I feel the urge to make a rope out of the blankets I found...
I finally found a small, secure house. In the surrounding houses I found enough stuff to close the windows. I expected it would be difficult but in each house I found their owners turned to monsters. I don't know how many people I killed. Men, woman and even kids.
Although I have a rather safe place to sleep, I feel like if each minute a small part of me dies.
While accessing a house I cut both of my forearms on broken glas, I aches like hell. And finally, I accidentally triggered an alarm and there are hundreds of zombies around.
I can't hear that sirene anymore. Hopefully, its battery dies soon. I feel like a  kid when I press my face into the pillow just not to hear that terrible noise of zombies scratching on the outside of my shelter.
I'd like to drink the whisky to raise my mood but I need to keep it to clean my wounds.
I spotted a zombie waiting on my front door. I thought it would be the best to kill it, but I didn't recognize another one just around the corner.
I killed both but I'm heavily wounded. I don't think I will make it.

Project Zomboid is An amazing game.
Sometimes I even forget that it is still in Early Access.
The reason for this is because there are so much different items and most things look very polished. In Project Zomboid you take the role of a lone survivor (unless you are playing multiplayer) and you have to survive. In this game everything is against you, almost nothing is in your favour. You have to swap bandages every few minutes in order to not get infection, you need to sleep, can't carry too much, get tired from running too much, can get sick from the cold or get heatstroke and you even have to relieve yourself of boredness.
This game is a very nice addition to the zombie genre in my opinion. The developers are working on this game and there are a few updates every now and then. A must have for any zombie survival game enthusiasts.

The basic premise of Five Nights at Freddy's demands the player spend the vast majority of the game inactive. The diminishing power supply - the resource used for protection - actually incentivizes sitting still and waiting. Not that there's much that can be done, electricity or no. There are two doors, a light for each door, and series of security cameras to check. There's not even an in-game menu, esc just closes the game entirely. But surprisingly, inactivity and the helplessness that develops from that lack of options, only strengthens the inevitable jump scare. While Five Nights at Freddy's is very clear about what it has to offer, it does bear repeating: this is not a game that lends itself to speculation or any sort of terror that would outlast the experience; anticipation and jump scares are all that can be found here.

Some of the hardest levels were in the first half of the game, and usually I'd end up playing through a lot of levels, getting stuck on one for a while, and then going back to having no issues for another round of stages. This trend kept up from probably some 15-20 levels into the game until the very end.
2. Time constraint seems unnecessary, there are a few stages where it's the only real enemy because a titan is so durable and takes too long to kill. Often this is coupled with not being given proper firepower (if you don't have at least one of the heavy fire or rapid fire, you're probably underpowered). Other times getting up close to destroy the boss the easy way results in taking massive damage.
3. The "bullet hell" part is only partially true. The problem that presents itself in this game is that you have a relatively limited viewing field, as opposed to full information, and you have a pretty fat hitbox. So the only thing this has in common with a bullet hell game is that there's stuff everywhere, but more often than not it's more a matter of luck than skill that you dodge it.
4. Damage is wack, yo. Lasers do 25% of your health and nothing else comes close to that, but you also have no invicibility frames and can be spam-combo'd from full health to zero in milliseconds. It's way too punishing for a single mistake with how long some of the fights can go on.
5. Terrain is often unwieldly/unfitting. Any vertical arena is automatically trash. Any arena comprised mostly of narrow straightaways or circles is automatically trash. Some of the arenas are too small for the bosses you have to fight. Some of them are too big. Not every arena is bad, but a lot of them have issues. There were also many instances where I found myself stuck in terrain with no way to get out (thus dying shortly after as all the drones caught up to me). Even got stuck inside a titan once or twice.
At its core the game can be pretty fun when it's not trying to be stupidly demanding of the player (here's looking at you, level 48, and your probably-a-typo time condition + awful arena) but it leaves me in a sour mood as I sit here having just completed the final boss, and practically makes me say "hell with it" to that last achievement. It's not worth it.
Also, $15 for a game with little actual "design" to speak of aside from some great graphic designs that get old a few hours in and gameplay mostly consisting of somewhat samey fights might be a bit steep, I got it 75% off and felt I got my money's worth there at least, but at full price it's probably too bare bones for most people.

Unlocking the frame rate:
Locate the ROEngine.ini inside: "C:\Users\User\Documents\My Games\RedOrchestra2\ROGame\Config" open ROEngine with Notepad.
Locate a parameter that looks like this:
bSmoothFrameRate=TRUE
MinSmoothedFrameRate=22
MaxSmoothedFrameRate=62
Set "MaxSmoothedFrameRate=62" to "MaxSmoothedFrameRate=144" - I've used 144 as an example.
Note: Setting "bSmoothFrameRate=FALSE" will uncap the limit but you will only be able to get 90 frames.
Find the remaining MaxSmoothedFrameRate lines (use Ctrl + f) and set their values to the desired amount (there are 2 MaxSmoothedFrameRate and 2 bSmoothFrameRate to edit).
Now test using either the steam FPS overlay or alternatively open the console ingame with "~" and type in "Stat FPS".

I cannot recommend this game enough. It has become (in ALPHA, mind you) my absolute FAVORITE Indie game. It's a Rogue-like (which means randomized, perma-deaths, all that good jazz), Dungeon Crawler, RPG, Tower Defense AND OFFENSE. You protect your Power Crystal from enemies lurking within the dungeon, while simultaniously branching out into the randomized dungeon, placing defenses and slaughtering monsters as you go... Did I mention there is no way to know what you are about to encounter? Yep, you never know what's behind the next door (which is especially scary when you are presented with three or more doors, since any of them can lead to your demise if you aren't lucky), which adds tension and a great sense of satisfaction when you find more blueprints to build new defenses or finding a treasure chest with equipment for your party of heroes. The party system definitely lives up to the greatness of the game's concept. You are given two random heroes to start with (You can, however, find more heroes throughout the dungeon to recruit), and you basically give them commands (kinda like FTL, where you don't really have REAL control over where they go in the room, but you tell them to go from room to room, where they automatically do things such as repairing defenses or fighting enemies.) It's a really simple concept, but in the thick of enemy swarms it certainly makes you think quickly and react fast, commanding your heroes like a pro. Okay, so I've already gone on about the gameplay and concepts (which, if I haven't already stated my feelings, I LOVE THEM), but the real show-stealer for me is the QUALITY of the world, characters, effects, and sounds. This game is GORGEOUS, like a modern day retro classic. The visuals are pixel art, but done in such a stylized way it's impossible not to stare at it's beauty. And the sound design is OFF THE CHARTS! It's so awesome that they are actually bothering to give you the soundtrack when the game officially launches. Not to mention, if you buy the Founder's Pack (which I did), you can actually vote on what features you feel are the most important for them to implement throughout it's development, which is awesome! They are also listening to player feedback and working to make everything exactly the way that we the gamers want them to be. In a word, the developer is awesome. I fully support Amplitude and this project has my Bender-Certified Seal of Awesomeness and Approval.

An absolute treasure.  Cuphead is a run-and-gun style game modeled after Contra but with more emphasis on boss battles than levels.  The bosses all have multiple phases, multiple attacks within each phase, and different patterns of movement to go with them.  This ties rather wonderfully with the game's gorgeous Golden Age of Animation art style.  Like an early Disney, Tex Avery or Fleischer Brothers cartoon things can get wonderfully weird at the drop of a hat.  It's a perfect fit, and the whimsical tone goes along with the steep challenge curve to create an atmosphere of fun.  Even dying is fun.  I should know, I've done it about 200 times (actually closer to 300 by now, I think) and while I haven't finished the game yet I can heartily recommend it to anyone who has played Contra and loved it but thought to themselves, "You know, I wish this looked a lot more like Steamboat Willie and had giant boxing frogs that turned into killer slot machines."  It's a highly specific request, I admit, but Cuphead delivers.
I don't know what the brothers Moldenhauer will do next, but they've done something truly great here, and I hope this is just the first triumph of many for them.

When this game was first announced, I didn't think I would buy it. It looked charming, yes, but I wasn't sold on the gameplay and $20 is on the higher end of non-AAA titles. I ended up giving in to hype to play coop with a friend, and then started a new game solo, eventually completing the entire thing (Expert mode included).
Cuphead is beautiful. The graphics look gorgeous and the audio is a great mix of mellow to fastpaced with plenty of character for each track. I played using a PS4 controller and the controls were very responsive. Occasionally it's hard to do certain button combos at the same time, but that challenge is included with most run-n-gun platformers.
The game is definitely hard. I won't call it Dark Souls because it's not, but it does deliver a rush in the same way Dark Souls does. Each new boss is a new foe standing in your way. They have their own patterns and phases, which both require the player to pay attention and think quickly to dodge incoming attacks whilst dishing out their own. These fights don't take long, so it's very easy to see improvements between deaths. You can feel yourself improving and it feels amazing when you get the victory K.O.
You are provided with an assortment of different projectiles, super moves, and passive buffs which you can purchase in game to help defeat bosses. I wouldn't call it customization but it's very nice to have some options. It switches up your play style considerably in some cases, making the game feel easier or harder.
The story is simple. The game tells you what you need to do and you go out into the world to do it. Is it the perfect story? No. Does it work? Yes. Cuphead doesn't dwell on the story too much. Because of this, I would like to note that you are buying the gameplay. That's where the fun is. The story is merely complimentary to the gameplay.
Overall, I highly recommend giving this game a shot if you enjoy games (like Dark Souls) that reward overcoming difficult challenges. Cuphead is a gem that should be experienced regardless of your game preference because there is simply nothing like it right now. Nothing else has so much style and pizazz, while also keeping the game fun and difficult. This is a must-buy for 2017..

I really wish steam had a neutral rating.  This isn't a bad game, but at just 2 hours it is incredibly small for the price.  It has one concept (time only moves when you move, which isn't actually true; enemies and bullets still move even when standing still, just very slowly), but it doesn't do much with it.  The campaign levels are short, and the challenge levels all happen in the same arena.  The tiny story tries to be artsy and profound but comes across as just vague nonsense.  I have a feeling it was made for the VR platform and a lot is lost when playing on PC.
The game is also headache-inducing because the environment is predominately white, and there is very little to break that up.  Movement is slow and herky-jerky, which makes manuvering painfully frustrating, but it's required because levels are designed so you can't take two steps without being in someone's line of fire, and the game requires precision movement to dodge enemies and bullets.  The levels are disconnected and have nothing to do with one another, which doesn't help the story at all because it doesn't feel like a coherent whole.
The developers had a decent idea, and I think it could have been better if the story mode had been better.  Without that, everything is kinda pointless.  It's not bad as a proof-of-concept, as the gameplay is challenging, satisfying, and stands on its own, but a single gimmick can only take a game so far.

The Steam version has one huge advantage and that's having some of the best looking achievements around. If you 100% the game, you get a full alphabet of achievements that you can use to write things in the achievement showcases on your profile. It's no simple task to get them all, but it does give you something fun to use after you are done. TL:DR - If you're looking for a more casual RTS - This isn't it.
So, I can see how this would be something many people could like. It is Star Wars after all. But after playing for a good 5 hours, I can tell that this is not a Star Wars game that I like. Which is very rare for me.
My experience with it so far has been pretty horrendous, mainly through seemingly cheating AI mechanics and sudden difficulty spikes. Naturally, I was playing on Easy, and I'm not great at RTS, but I sort of assumed it would be more like C&C where you would have time to build up your forces and then assualt the enemy. Its not like that at all. My experiences come from C&C Red Alert and Generals and I've also played a fair amount of Shogun Total War. My issue I feel is that the time scale of the game literally leaves you behind within 30 seconds.
In Galactic CQ, I am frequently being raided and out-gunned within the first 5 minutes of play. The AI steam rolls as it doesn't seem to be confined to the amount of actions a human could physically decide upon and take. The AI is so precise and clinical in its processes, that within the first 5 Galactic days, the Rebellion already has amased an economy 5 times greater than my own. I've been through forums and such and there seems to be no real answers about why this game is so different in play style to C&C or Shogun. But I feel its the fact that the AI moves so fast.
Personally I was looking for a more casual Star Wars C&C clone. This is not what this game is, unless you're already good at such game. I feel like I would have enjoyed it more if I had time to learn and not be swept off the game board almost immeditly by huge fleets which can't physically have been created with only a starting credit cap if 5K. Inexperience is also a deciding factor. The tutorials are decent, but they don't really provide you with the load of how much you have to do and organise. Also, the reinforcement mechanic which the player is forced to use, but the AI can happily spawn tanks etc against you... is just broken.
Also, don't bother playing the expansion. The 3rd faction is so OP that there is literally no point, unless you like seeing all of your "owned" worlds, completely corrupted and leeched within 30 seconds.
Just glad I bought it on sale. If we consider £1 for 1 hour of play-time, I'd say the game at least achieved that.

This is an interesting twist on the Zombie Survival Genre. Unlike other games where you randomly generate in the middle of nowhere, and have only your clothes on your back while you scavenge around barren towns and buildings to try and find something as simple as food, while hoping some random jerk doesn't snipe you as a fresh spawn. In this game, you have an abundance of food and drink, Don't let my lack of playtime on Steam fool you.. I've spent a bit of time with this game, and watched tons of videos to add.
Your character can only see where they are facing.. giving you that feeling of having to constantly look over your shoulder to see if anyone (or thing) is approaching from behind. This game also takes things to a little more of a realistic level: You can pull sheets off of beds and place them over windows to act as curtains to avoid zombies looking in and seeing you while you're scavenging or sleeping. Sound is also your enemy in this game.. If you sprint, zombies will hear it. If you break a window to enter a building (and possibly trigger a house alarm), zombies will hear it and swarm that area. If you fire a gun.. an entire horde will close in on you.
The only thing I would recommend be changed in this game, is the blocky control system. Moving your character and using objects is fine, but the interface itself is a bit blunky; ie - accessing your inventory quickly while being surrounded by zombies and trying to loot a crate for that desperately needed axe to start caving heads in.. Aside from that, this is a very nicely polished survival game, and is substantially more fun with playing with other people. Solo is a blast, as well.
But don't expect to stay alive forever.. in the world of Project Zomboid.. there is only one driving question.. "How will you die?"
